newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks defy Dow, surge on auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks defy Dow, surge on auction hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks shrugged off a sharp fall on Wall Street to increase earlier gains and close up on Tuesday on bargain-hunting amid forecasts that interest rates would break with their recent upward trend, dealers said.
"Gains were very firm, the market discounted positive factors like expected falls in domestic primary rates," said Diego Candano, equity research director at the IXE brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 36.50 points, or 0.97 percent, at 3,797.05.
"There is also a more widespread consensus the Federal Open Market Committee will not raise U.S. rates (on March 25) and the drug certification row has run out of steam," a dealer said.

A Reuters survey of nine Mexico City money market traders showed they predicted an average assignment rate of 22.20 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes. This would be a fall of 97 basis points since last week.
News broke in late trade that a U.S. Senate proposal to decertify Mexico's anti-drug efforts had been dropped in negotiations with government officials.

Some dealers meanwhile said favorable industrial output figures released mid-morning helped bolster share prices. The Finance Ministry announced industrial output in January had climbed 8.8 percent from year-ago figures.
"The market was very selective. Dealers picked up low-priced blue chips. I feel the industrial output figures fueled buying," a desk trader said.
Trading volume was unremarkable at 75.2 million shares, but picked up late in the day as some foreign buyers entered the market. An initial public offering by Minsa accounted for 14.2 million shares.
Corn flour firm Minsa C shares closed unchanged from their issue price of 11.19 pesos.
Candano did not expect a firm rally until April.
"We would have to firmly break through 3,850 points to think or a rally, which we nonetheless do not rule out in April. For now, at least, we confirmed a floor at 3,750 points," he said.
"Buyers won't really step in until April, as many prefer to go liquid over the long (Easter) weekend," he added.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on March 21, 27 and 28.
A total of 105 stocks changed hands on the broad market, of which gains outnumbered slides 53 to 32.
Financial group Banacci was a prominent gainer, up 80 centavos to 18.80 pesos, followed by food company Grupo Corvi, which gained 19 centavos to 4.50 pesos on speculative buying, traders said.
"Banacci was oversold, but it had sound fundamentals," a trader said.
Traders also drew attention to the Serfin financial group, which declined five centavos to 3.45 pesos.
Serfin announced during trade that it was about to finalize a partial sale to "an Asian bank," but news of a 1996 net loss totalling almost seven billion pesos was still ringing in traders' ears.
"The market had discounted the Serfin deal. It was the only viable option, so there was little reaction," a desk trader said.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the prominent sliders' list .PL.MX, off six centavos to 40 centavos, followed by its tourism arm Situr, which fell three centavos to 24 centavos.
((--Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
